utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Dr. Turkusic, I have only one more question for you. While you were present on the ground to investigate the Markale II shelling incident, did you make any observations about the hardness of the ground where the shell impacted?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: The shell fell on the road, that is, firm asphalt surface which is customary in urban areas. At the point of impact - and that always happens when a shell falls on a hard surface - there was a clear rose pattern with shrapnel traces and a symmetry that could be used excellently for determining the angle of descent, the azimuth, and also the angle of descent of the shell itself. So that is what I have to say about the surface.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: In particular, was -- would there be anything to distinguish the shell -- the area where this shell landed from, for example, a pedestrian path?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Well, places that we could call pedestrian paths are surfaces that are softer and a shell usually leaves a deeper trace or impact or, like in Markale I, the stabiliser that is part of the shell and it is a passive body during the explosion. It was speeded up by the vacuum that occurs because of the explosion and it impacted the ground even asphalt because it is softer, it is meant for pedestrians.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Harbour. I'm afraid that I did not fully understand the last answer. Could you -- neither did I fully understand the question to be quite honest. Let's look at both. Witness, you said where the shell landed was firm asphalt surface. The -- a pedestrian path is usually composed of what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood the question to be to describe the difference between a shell falling on a very firm surface or if it were to fall on a surface which is actually a pedestrian path. It is a well-known thing that in -- well, that's it, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was trying to split up various questions because if you compare the two it's always good to know where we know what is the composition of the surface where the shell landed. You said it was firm asphalt. We do not know, however, although you qualified it as softer, what is usually the composition of a pedestrian path.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a question of pure physics, actually. We can have two surfaces that are of the same firmness -- I beg your pardon, equally hard. However, one can be solid and impenetrable and another one can be less hard and penetrable, although their surfaces are equally hard. So that is the basic difference between very hard and firm surfaces on which there is heavy traffic, where automobiles move, and so on. And also, there can be others that can have a firm surface but are otherwise not that hard because they are meant for pedestrians. If a shell were to fall on both surfaces, although both of them are the same on the surface, they are equally hard, there's going to be an elastic impact and perhaps the fuse is going to bounce off. And in another case there can be this plastic clash or impact, as we say in physics. And then the stabiliser of the shell can pierce the surface where the shell fell. It is a well-known thing that the stabiliser of the shell, due to the explosion that occurred underneath it, where there was a vacuum, it can be accelerated additionally and it can impact the surface. Now there are two possibilities: If the surface is very firm, like in this case, then it bounces off; then there is this other possibility, that the surface is not hard enough and then the stabiliser literally sticks into it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you're talking about a vacuum due to the explosion underneath the stabiliser element of the explosion. Would the explosion only create a vacuum or would it also create a back-throwing force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ultra-fast explosions, like those of TNT, happen very -- within a very short span of time. And then there is an expansion, three-dimensional, pushing the parts of the shell that is bursting at that point in time. That is the moment when in the centre of the explosion, due to this effect of expansion, there is high vacuum. This high vacuum, of course, we're talking about only parts of seconds, it literally speeds up the stabiliser that is moving towards this vacuum. So it is accelerated additionally. As for the other effects on the surface, I've already described that. If you wish, I can make an analogy which would explain these two phenomena.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you can easily explain it for us, you are invited to do so. Whether we are --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very simply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether we are sufficient understanding to follow it is a matter still to be seen. Yes. Please --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You will, certainly. If you take a steel of same quality, you make a sheet 1 millimetre thick and a piece of sheet 10 millimetres thick and you take these two sheets that have equal firmness because we have the same steel, we fire from a handgun. The thin sheet can be pierced by the bullet and the thicker one cannot. So this is the analogy identical to the fall of a shell on a surface that is of equal firmness but different hardness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that. If it's only a thin layer, it may go through, whereas if it's a thick layer of the same material --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it may stop. Now, that does not yet answer my last question which was about the vacuum. You said the explosion itself would create a vacuum and therefore would speed up the stabiliser fin in its trajectory towards the centre of the explosion. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, apart from creating a vacuum at the centre of the explosion, would in the immediate vicinity of the explosion within centimetres, decimetres, would it also create a force away from the vacuum and throwing everything away from the centre of the explosion due to that explosion itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It has to do with the sequence of events. At the point of detonation, the area expands because that is how explosives operate, this sudden expansion tears the shell into small pieces and throws it away from the point of impact. Shortly afterwards the consequence is the vacuum by expanding the mass from this point outwards and this is where the pressure occurs. Since simultaneously the tail fin of the shell which is rather massive and has its inertia and speed, it is moving towards the centre where the vacuum is, it gains additional speed. As a result, the tail fin impacts on the surface at a slightly higher speed than the speed of the shell itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it is not thrown away as a first -- as a first effect of the explosion, like the shrapnel pieces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is sucked in because the shrapnel have already left the location. They were pushed away by the explosion and they have already gone away from the place where the vacuum is created, while the tail fin, due to the fact that it's still being on the move, comes under the influence of the vacuum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the tail fin initially is not subject to the same force which pushes back the pieces of shrapnel. It is also on the outside part of the explosive body of the -- body of the shell, is it not subject to such a force throwing it and if it is in certain speed perhaps reducing the speed of the tail fin due to this explosive effect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The tail fin of the shell, a stabiliser which is a pipe-shaped part, it has fins at its end which are physically attached to it and they create a physical body. Both the pipe and the fins make a stabiliser which is a mechanical part and that is a passive part of the shell. Its role is only during the firing and the trajectory of the shell. When it comes to the explosion, the entire stabiliser has no active role in the impact of the shell. It has no intended role.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honour. I don't know if the Prosecution received a list of our documents for the cross-examination. I was on line with our Case Manager and I don't know if the complete list was sent or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: We haven't received the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you will receive it very soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Hopefully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Otherwise you're invited to make a hard copy and provide it to Ms. Harbour. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Turkusic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On behalf of the Defence of General Mladic, I'm going to put some questions to you. My first question is this: When we discussed some issues without you, I would like to know whether you have been called here as an expert witness or as a fact witness.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I believe I was called to appear as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your testimony, are you presenting things that are not personally known to you but come from second-hand sources?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: If I'm doing that, I always emphasise that. If I'm not familiar with something myself, I will say so. If there is something that I'm not certain about, something in our reports, I will always say "most probably" or "most likely."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel kindly speak into the microphone. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm trying.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The documents that you have - and you know which documents I'm talking about - include the documents that you yourself did not create?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: That is correct. However, creating documents is a relative notion. We operated as a team --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I am talking about documents primarily issued by the SUP, by public security stations, and that sort of documents that you did not take part in any way whatsoever or your colleagues from the KDZ.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. And these documents have been attached.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You explained today the occurrence of vacuum. Now I'm going to take a slightly reverse approach. I'm going to ask you about the charge. Does it have any effect on the fact whether the stabiliser will become embedded into the surface or not?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Standard charge of the shells is TNT which is initiated by fuse with the booster accentuated explosion and I think that this is a standard charge that is applicable throughout the world since the Second World War. My direct answer to your question would be: It has no effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't want this to remain unclear. Maybe I did not phrase my question properly. What I meant was whether the shell has primary and secondary and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please pause between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you to make a pause between question and answer. And could I also invite you, when you're talking about the charge, you most likely are talking about the explosive charge and we have two charges. I think the one is the explosives within the body of the shell and the other is the charge -- the propelling charge for the shell. Could we always try to make -- if you would agree that we have these two different charges, always to clearly express which charge you are referring to, either in question or in the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In accordance with the Judge's instructions, I'm going to ask you about the propelling charge. Does it have any effect on the stabiliser being embedded into the surface?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does. If the angle of firing, which is a little below 90, if it is activated in such a manner that the charge is being intensified due to a longer range, the shell will reach a higher elevation due to its trajectory. From such elevation, the shell will continue to flow towards the ground under the influence of gravity. If it falls from a higher height, its acceleration becomes higher. The sum of all these accelerations, the speed of the stabiliser additionally increased by the vacuum would create a stronger effect by its being embedded into the surface regardless of what kind of surface we are talking about and we mentioned various examples of that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters from the French booth are kindly asking that the -- that both persons slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The interpreters are again asking us not only to make a pause between question and answer, but also to slow down your speed of speech. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You will notice that I am making a pause after your answer, waiting for interpretation. It's not that I am being rude, but this is the procedure and I am sure that you are familiar with it. You answered in a specific way, but I'm going to ask you this: If we take that the angle of the mortar is 50 degrees, the mortar barrel, and we fire a shell with the first charge and the sixth charge, is the angle of the shell going to be different in that case?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: The angle of firing ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Since this is a parabola of slanted round, the angle of firing will be the same in both cases. There is some minor difference in the descent angle as well, taking into consideration all the relevant factors, like the height, wind, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under such circumstances, if we have identical angles and when there is no increase of the descent angle, will the charge have any influence? The propelling charge, will it have any influence on whether the tail fin is going to be embedded in the surface or not?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: In my view, it would have relatively little influence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could I ask for a clarification. If the propelling charge is considerably higher, let's say 6 instead of 1, you said if the angle of fire is still the same, 50 degrees, would the speed of the projectile be considerably higher upon firing if you would use 6 instead of 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it would. The higher the charge, the propelling force marked by G which is the multiplication of the earth's gravity, if you have more charges you have more acceleration. The shell will fly out of the barrel at an increased speed consistent with an increased level of charge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would this have a result on the speed of impact of that shell? Would it also -- would it also arrive at the point of impact with an increased speed compared to a shell with only one propelling charge -- a propelling charge of 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since with higher charge the shell will reach a higher vertical elevation, then during free fall it will travel towards the ground for a longer time and it will be subjected to the gravity of a higher level and consequently would reach the ground at a higher speed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And would have -- would that have an impact on that depth, if at all, from which the tail fin would embed in the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it would in terms that the stabiliser would travel at a higher speed, but it all depends on the surface that it is landing upon. If you have extremely solid surface, it will have no impact or influence whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but if the surface would be the same for a propelling charge of 1 compared to a propelling charge of 6, it would have an impact on the speed of arrival at impact and would have an effect on how the shell would embed in the ground if the surface again is the same in this comparison. Would you agree to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understood you correctly, if we have an extremely hard surface which is practically inpenetrable for the tail fin, as was the case in Markale II where we had an asphalt surface, the speed of the fall of the shell and the possible embedding of the tail fin into the surface would end up in this way: The stabiliser would at any rate bounce off the surface in an elastic way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I was not referring to any specific example. I was just referring to the theoretical aspects of the speed of firing of the projectile and the speed of arrival upon impact of the projectile. But Mr. Lukic will now put further questions to you. Mr. Lukic, as a result of the answers I received on my previous questions, could we always also clearly distinguish between what happens in a specific situation and what happens in general. Because I understood the answers of the witness that with such a hard surface that the speed might not be of great influence on embedding, but perhaps with a different surface it might have such an impact. So we always have to clearly distinguish between a specific situation and between questions which are put in general terms. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us just deal with this then. Is it correct that in your view this would not be influenced in any way if the surface is susceptible to the tail fin falling into it, that is to say that the charge would not affect that in any way?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: If the surface is a thin layer of asphalt relatively soft or if it's a patch of grass, then if the shell were to arrive at a higher speed it would embed itself into the surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say "higher speed," do you mean a bigger angle of descent or a higher charge?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I mean a higher charge and that directly has to do with the speed of descent.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have to insist on a clear use of the language. "Speed" is not the same as "angle of descent." "Speed" is not the same as "a higher charge." They may all be related, but the speed is the result of the charge, the propelling charge, used and the angle of fire which is related to an angle of descent. Would you agree with that, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So therefore let's try to use the words as precise as possible, not mixing up different concepts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It seems that I didn't quite understand something here. Does the charge have anything to do with the angle of descent and the angle of firing -- well, that's clear. Does the charge have anything to do with the angle of descent, that is to say, the angle at which the shell hits the surface?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: The firing of a shell, a mortar shell, substantially differs from a projectile fired from a rifle or a cannon. It's rather similar to a howitzer, though. The shell is fired up into the air and it falls at a relatively large angle. Ballistics relates this directly to gravity. During the flight of ascent of the shell and also as the shell descends from the maximum highest point as it moves towards the ground. So the launching charge is bigger and then there will be a greater height involved and then practically at the same angle of firing the shell will fall on the ground. If we were to draw the trajectory of different charges, we would have a group of curves that have the same points where they start and end, but the height is different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you one question in this respect. If I fire a projectile with the same angle of firing that is -- well, let's say, 60 degrees, is it your testimony that the projectile would travel just as far if fired with one propelling charge compared to how far it would travel - I'm not talking about altitude - how far it would travel with six propelling charges? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said: "... the same points where they start and end ..." But for different charges at the same angle of fire they would not end -- they would not end at the same place. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon. Slip of the tongue. With a completely identical firing angle, we would have different ranges with all of these trajectories. A higher charge would cause a parabola that would exceed the previous ones in terms of distance and in terms of height.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic, unless you think it would be time for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe we have couple of more minutes, but maybe it would be wise to be able to provide the Prosecution with the list. Obviously they haven't received it yet. We have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we could take the break now, as you wish. I think we are one hour on our way since the previous break, so that is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For us it's an excellent time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we would ask the usher to escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we'll take a break and we'll resume at 20 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Lukic, the Defence has expressed some concerns about the expert type of evidence this witness gives. At the same time, you are further exploring not only the evidence of matters the witness observed himself but also in this expert field.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Challenging the knowledge of the witness and obviously it's very poor in this field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I'm not expressing any view on that yet. That's your judgement on poverty or not. At the same time, of course the witness testifies here, it's evidence, so whether -- and I'm not in any way -- and we discussed it during the break among the Judges, I'm not stopping you in any way of asking these questions which are related to the statement, but at the same time the Chamber considers the value of this witness primarily to be found in matters he observed himself and investigated himself. Of course it's perhaps impossible to separate it from his experience and his skills. But a focus on that might assist the Chamber very much. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will go through the witness statement and I will start right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Turkusic, you are a doctor of chemical technology?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: A doctor of chemistry, doctor of science in chemistry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During the war -- actually, what kind of training did you have before the war and during the war?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: An engineer. I was an engineer of chemical technology.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: An engineer. That's why I was wondering about this. Actually, I don't know if you have your statement with you. Would it be helpful if you had your statement before you in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I can provide that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Immediately on the second page, that is Roman numeral II, 1992-1994, you said that you joined the 1st Dobrinja Brigade. At that time you lived in Dobrinja as well; right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was commander of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Ismet --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was it Ismet Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many APC's did the Dobrinja Brigade have?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that, maybe one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You don't know about more than one?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From the Dobrinja Brigade you moved to the centre for specific production?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The centre for that production, military production, was at the faculty of science and -- the mechanical faculty; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the centre for military production, you worked on the manufacturing of hand-grenades and tromblones; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where did you manufacture shells for rifle grenades?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Rifle grenades, regardless of whether they are purely explosive or shape-charged, we manufactured them at the faculty of mechanical engineering. That's the building right next door. The parts that were manufactured there were assembled into a final product.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the centre for military production you worked with Mr. Berko Zecevic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. He was at the centre, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He was head of the centre, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: It was Faik, Faik Kulovac or Kulovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic was one of the senior personnel there; right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Within this centre you also manufactured chemical rifle grenades; right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Now we're going to try to refresh your memory a bit and I'm going to show you 1D1198 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we move to that document, could the witness explain to the Chamber what "shape-charged" exactly means? We just don't know. You used the expression. He said: "... regardless of whether they are purely explosive or shape-charged ..." What -- could you explain what do you mean by "shape-charged"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me first answer to the first part of your question concerning shaped charge. These shells are fired from a rifle. So you have a bullet in the rifle without the bullet itself, there's only gunpowder. After triggering the pressure created by the powder, there is a grenade which is attached to the top of the barrel and that is how it is launched. Generally speaking, this is a rifle grenade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a question --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, according to the structure it can be a hand-grenade, a fragmentation grenade that produces an identical effect, or its structure can be such that upon impact it has a piercing effect to an obstacle or an armour. Due to the low level of charge in both cases these grenades are of relatively low strength and are actually used only in infantry battles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a question, please. At page 69, line 22, you are interpreted as having said the following: "So you have a bullet in the rifle without the bullet itself ..." I don't understand that. How do you have a bullet without the bullet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was clear. If you imagine a rifle bullet and you take the lead ball out of it and you press the top you have only the gunpowder charge inside the bullet; however, this gunpowder charge during firing creates pressure that will eject the grenade from the top of the rifle and the rifle grenade is shaped in such a way that it has a tail fin similar to that of a mortar shell in order to fly through the air, it has a very small range and very small power of destruction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where you said a bullet without a bullet, could you also express it as a cartridge without a bullet mounted on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Without the ball. Practically, that makes it a manoeuvre ammunition by the way it looks, by the way it is constructed, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have a translation of this document, at least we were unable to locate it, so I'm going to use it to a limited extent and I'm going to ask the witness to read for us what this is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please read the date in the incoming stamp, who the recipient is, and what kind of document this is. Who is the sender?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Main Staff of the armed forces, the centre for special-purpose production, 1st of September, 1992. The date of the document itself is the date much before I joined the unit. The total number of copies, three. The title is: The production of war assets in war conditions certain aspects of unhindered production, September 1992, which is two years before I joined the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did you join the centre for special-purpose production?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We know that this centre was disbanded in December 1994 -- 1992.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I think I joined the KDZ in 1994. I spent a relatively short time working at the centre in September 1992 -- I don't have that date in my memory. I don't think it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us look now at the next page. You can see here the list of -- it says in its operations so far, the centre of special-purpose production produced the following war assets, second bullet point: Chemical rifle grenades.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: What is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does this remind you that during your work there, chemical rifle grenades were indeed manufactured and do you know what their charge was?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I was not involved in their production and I don't know anything about their charges.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There's also special rifle grenade ammunition produced.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: What are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Five -- fifth bullet point which says special rifle grenade ammunition.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: All right. What is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that your description that for the firing of rifle grenades manoeuvre ammunition was being used is incorrect, that there is also a detonator cap in the special rifle grenade ammunition?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: No. It is a well-known fact that during war games, bullets without balls are being used which only have a noisy effect of firing. The weight in grams of gunpowder in these cartridges is irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please slow down. We --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the difference between the manoeuvre ammunition and the rifle grenade ammunition basically is this: The manoeuvre ammunition doesn't have the weight of gunpowder as a relevant factor, whereas in special rifle grenade ammunition it is very important how many grams of gunpowder are in every cartridge. It is by precision weighing and re-combining the gunpowder in manoeuvre ammunition and re-filling it with gunpowder one can get a standard rifle grenade and that is what is called special rifle grenade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was some special type of gunpowder used?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: There is no special type of gunpowder. You have gunpowder for rocket motors in the form of sticks. There are gunpowder for firing, but the differences between guns and mortars are only slight. The grains are a bit higher and nitrocycline nitrocyloid [as interpreted] gunpowder is a newer one as opposed to the old smoke gunpowder which has completely been made redundant.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now look at page 3 of this document. This is this portion which contains signature. Does this refresh your memory that the chief of the centre was Mr. Berko Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: The chief of the centre for research and development.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So this chief of CNP is not enough?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Well, research and development is a subarea.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise Mr. Zecevic's signature?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: It seems to be his signature, but I haven't seen it in practice too often in order to be able to recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In order for us to establish the time-line, would you agree that you moved to the KDZ from this centre?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did any of your colleagues from this centre went to work for the KDZ?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: One of my colleagues went to the CSB KDZ in Sarajevo and I think I was the only one who joined the KDZ of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, no speaking aloud. If you want to consult with counsel, brief consultations at low volume are allowed, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Low volume, Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After you went to the KDZ, did you continue your co-operation with Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you invite him to attend the investigation after the Markale I incident in February of 1994?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to move to paragraph 9 of your statement, where you say that you never encountered a situation, that's the last sentence in this paragraph, that you absolutely never encountered any credible information that would lead to a conclusion that the Bosnian government forces were deliberately targeting civilians in Sarajevo. Are you familiar with the evidence given by Mr. Herenda who said and described some specific situations when upon orders of his superiors he fired at the Sarajevo population inside the territory controlled by the ABH?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I have never heard such a statement. In case it is completely true, it does not in any case refute the last sentence of my paragraph 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you obtain information that on the 9th of November, 1993, from the territory controlled by the ABH two shells were fired at ZAVNOBIH building when four boys and a teacher were --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Lukic please repeat whether they were killed or wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you're invited to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to repeat my question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the last part. Four boys and a teacher were wounded or killed?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Killed. Could you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This assertion presented in the form of a question is something that I am hearing for the first time and I personally believe that this is only part of a propaganda campaign that goes always hand in hand with a war by twisting the facts and this is also a form of ammunition that is used in any war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you would have answered the question by saying that you hear for the first time from this. If you do not know anything else, you could not possibly express any opinion about whether it's propaganda or not. These general opinions are not assisting the Chamber. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at Exhibit P497. That's a Prosecution exhibit. We need page 5 in B/C/S and page 1 in English because along with photo number 5 we only have the text in English. In your opinion, where did this mortar shell come from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The exhibit not to be shown to the public because it's under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From up or down? And let me tell you this, the street is -- just a moment, Safeta Hadzica 102. So this is area that is under the control of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: The question remains as you had put it. First of all, why do you claim that this is a mortar shell?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you disagree, do correct me.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of shell this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Irrespective of type, can you tell us whether this shell hit that wall in this case in such a way that the back part of the shell was underneath the shell or --

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Underneath judging by the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We just have a little bit time left. Now I'd like to ask you the following: When you carried out investigations -- well, first of all, did you often go to the scene itself?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: As far as war conditions allowed and since no such investigations were carried out in previous wars, this was the case relatively often.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you personally go out on to the scene or your colleagues -- actually, my question was whether you spent more time on the ground or in the lab?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I cannot tell. I cannot assess that. Given the war dynamic, I was everywhere, I and my colleagues, and different teams were established, different combinations. Reports were started and finished, but at any rate we worked as a team consisting of a variety of experts. So we checked each other, supplemented each other's information, and tried to leave a report, an analysis, that would be as faithful as possible with regard to anything that we dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is the end of our working day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, could I ask one question. I think I understood the testimony, but just to be sure about that. When we looked at this picture Mr. Lukic asked you whether the back part of the shell was underneath the shell. I think you said underneath judging by the picture. Did you mean to say from what you see on this picture that the tail end of the shell must have been lower than the point where the shell impacted on the wall? Is that how I have to understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely. However, I have this reservation in terms of this being a picture of an incident that I'm not aware of. However, judging by what we see in the picture, the shell would have come from down conditionally speaking. Although it is possible that such traces can be left. In many cases there are ricochets, so different projectiles leave different traces, but judging by this picture that's what it seems to be like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that it would have hit the wall in an upward direction. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the tail turned down, yes. Now, in the meantime, whether there was a ricochet or not, it amounts to speculation as far as I'm concerned. I could only speculate now. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We adjourn for the day and would like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30. Meanwhile, I instruct you that you should not speak or communicate with whomever about your testimony, whether that is testimony you've given today or whether that is testimony still to be given in the days following. If you've understood this well, you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar informs me that the translation -- the new translation, I think it was for the Republika Srpska Main Staff order, strictly confidential dated the 19th of November, that's P1968, has meanwhile been attached. We adjourn for the day and we will resume tomorrow -- Mr. Lukic, you don't want to resume tomorrow? No that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 28th of August, at 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom, III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 28th day of August, 2013, at 9.30 a.m.
